newsitem.title: CHINA: FEDEX,DHL SAY ASIAN BUSINESS UP.
newsitem.headline: FEDEX,DHL SAY ASIAN BUSINESS UP.

text.p: Express freight rivals of United Parcel Service in Hong Kong said they are enjoying an increase in business due to the strike by Teamster members which has crippled UPS operations in the U.S.

"We have seen a significant increase in packages all over our key markets in Asia and have also managed to maintain our service in spite of the increased volume surges," said Federal Express Corp, Asian marketing managing director,Raj Subramaniam told Reuters.
DHL International said everyone is getting more business because of UPS' problems.It added that it also ensuring existing customers did not suffer due to the sudden influx of new business.
"We are seeing an increase in business over the past couple of days but it has not gone crazy. Of course we like to see more business, especially express," a spokesman said.
Perry Chao, Hong Kong manager for UPS, said business was obviously not as good as before the strike. He hoped no-long term damage was being done.

"There is always a loss of business because some customers don't want to take the risk and look for someone else. But we still have our European and Asian operation still working, a chartered daily flight to the U.S. and customers are still giving us U.S. business " he added

"We have been communicating with our customers daily and they have been very understanding. We want to make sure they understand that it is only the U.S. which is on strike and everything else is normal," Chao said.

UPS said it has chartered a McDonnell Douglas DC-10 aircraft to replace its normal Boeing 747 flight between Hong Kong and Louisville as this has been has been grounded since pilots refuse to cross picket lines.
Chao declined to name the charter airline but Hong Kong airport sources said it is a DC-10-30F aircraft belong to Washington-based Gemini Air Cargo.

With the replacement DC-10 having less capacity than the 747 and current demand for trans-Pacific space at peak levels from Hong Kong, industry sources said UPS may have difficulty in securing additional space at short notice.
